topic-128-f-divergence-based-classificat.evolution: The examples span binary and directional Boltzmann models in the early 1990s, stochastic generative networks and bidirectional models in the 2010s, and recent marginalization, distribution embeddings, and constrained sampling. This is a widening collection of computational formulations, not evidence that one family universally replaces another.
openQuestions: How can efficient marginal queries retain reliable uncertainty in high dimensions?
Which consistency constraints improve sampling without restricting useful distributional structure?
topic-128-f-divergence-based-classificat.overview: These methods learn probability distributions that can generate data, answer conditional questions, and evaluate partially observed examples. The central challenge is making a flexible distribution computationally usable: exact likelihoods, posterior inference, and marginal probabilities can become expensive even when drawing a sample is easy. Representatives explore energy-based models, stochastic transitions, bidirectional inference, and explicitly learned marginals.
topic-128-f-divergence-based-classificat.title: Probabilistic Generative Modeling and Marginal Inference
topic-128-f-divergence-based-classificat.whyItMatters: A useful generator should support reasoning about missing information as well as realistic outputs. Choosing a training divergence or enforcing consistency between marginals can change both the statistical behavior and the cost of those operations.

topic-129-se-3-equivariant-convolution-a.evolution: Early representatives study stereo disparity, transparency, and object recognition from views. Recent papers add sparse-view radiance-field reconstruction and semantic feature distillation; 2026 examples extend weak supervision to radar motion and heterogeneous perception. The shared concern is extracting stable geometry from imperfect evidence across changing sensor settings.
openQuestions: How should models represent geometry that the available views cannot determine?
Can auxiliary supervision transfer without inheriting another sensor’s systematic errors?
topic-129-se-3-equivariant-convolution-a.overview: Scene reconstruction estimates depth, surfaces, occupancy, or motion from incomplete sensor observations. The represented work combines geometric constraints with learned priors, including monocular depth networks, radiance fields, foundation-model features, and information from different sensors. Sparse viewpoints make ambiguity central: several plausible scenes may explain the same images.
topic-129-se-3-equivariant-convolution-a.title: Scene Geometry from Sparse and Multimodal Observations
topic-129-se-3-equivariant-convolution-a.whyItMatters: Better geometry supports navigation and spatial understanding, while self-supervision reduces dependence on expensive three-dimensional labels. Cross-modal guidance can compensate for weak measurements, but must account for differences in scale, visibility, and sensing characteristics.

topic-130-a-deep-learning-approach-for-t.evolution: The historical examples include direct cardiac-signal classification and EEG analysis in the late 1980s and early 1990s. More recent work emphasizes unsupervised brain representations and large pretrained models. A 2026 benchmark highlights objective conflicts and negative transfer, showing that scale alone does not explain downstream performance.
openQuestions: Which pretraining objectives preserve neural information needed by diverse downstream tasks?
How can evaluation separate physiological generalization from recording-system familiarity?
topic-130-a-deep-learning-approach-for-t.overview: This topic learns representations of physiological recordings, especially brain activity measured across time, channels, and regions. Models must distinguish meaningful dynamics from variation in subjects, electrode placement, and recording conditions. Recent approaches connect local signal activity with functional relationships and use multiscale tokenization or attention to capture patterns at different spatial and temporal resolutions.
topic-130-a-deep-learning-approach-for-t.title: Brain and Biosignal Representation Learning
topic-130-a-deep-learning-approach-for-t.whyItMatters: Transferable representations could reduce labeled-data requirements for decoding tasks. Standardized evaluation is essential because improved results can reflect adaptation choices or dataset differences rather than a better general model.

topic-131-textit-himacon-discovering-hie.evolution: A 1995 example combines learned modules for gesture-guided pick-and-place. Later representatives study grasping and trajectory prediction. Recent work combines sequence imitation, reward learning, and large video-trained world models, broadening the available supervision beyond robot action labels without establishing a single inevitable development path.
openQuestions: When do human-video dynamics transfer to a robot’s actual action space?
How can long-horizon policies detect and recover from small execution errors?
topic-131-textit-himacon-discovering-hie.overview: Robot manipulation connects visual scene understanding with sequences of physical actions. These papers learn from demonstrations, pretrained visual features, and predictive world models, often decomposing long tasks into manageable stages. The challenge is to turn limited robot experience into policies that remain effective when objects, tasks, or embodiments change.
topic-131-textit-himacon-discovering-hie.title: Demonstration Learning and World Models for Robot Manipulation
topic-131-textit-himacon-discovering-hie.whyItMatters: Demonstrations can reduce difficult exploration, while predictive models allow an agent to assess possible consequences. Their value depends on accurately representing contact and action effects, not simply producing visually plausible future frames.

topic-132-4kagent-agentic-any-image-to-4.evolution: The examples begin with mean-field restoration of range images in 1988 and later Bayesian super-resolution. Neural deconvolution and encoder-decoder models appear in the 2010s; recent papers use stochastic dynamics and few-step consistency methods. Newer multi-view signal enhancement emphasizes reliability under very low signal-to-noise conditions.
openQuestions: How can restoration confidence distinguish recovered evidence from a learned prior’s plausible guess?
Can fast models remain reliable across unfamiliar mixtures of degradation?
topic-132-4kagent-agentic-any-image-to-4.overview: Restoration recovers useful structure from noisy, blurred, poorly illuminated, or low-resolution observations. The represented methods combine models of degradation with learned image or signal priors. Iterative optimization, neural architectures, diffusion processes, and consistency models offer different ways to balance reconstruction quality, computational cost, and resistance to artifacts.
topic-132-4kagent-agentic-any-image-to-4.title: Image Restoration and Reliable Signal Enhancement
topic-132-4kagent-agentic-any-image-to-4.whyItMatters: A sharper output is not necessarily a more faithful measurement. Effective restoration must preserve weak evidence while avoiding invented detail or excessive suppression, particularly when noise makes local features unreliable.

topic-133-mathrm-nit-scaling-simple-and-.evolution: Representatives include evolutionary architecture search in 2019, improved initialization, and primitive-level efficiency search in 2021. Later theory studies nonlinear in-context learning and pruning. A 2026 parameter-volume analysis examines why sensitive Boolean functions can occupy difficult-to-reach regions despite being expressible. These threads connect design experiments with increasingly specific explanations of training bias.
openQuestions: Which architectural changes improve learnability rather than only expressivity?
How far do tractable in-context-learning analyses predict behavior in full pretrained systems?
topic-133-mathrm-nit-scaling-simple-and-.overview: This topic studies why particular Transformer designs train efficiently and which functions their learning dynamics favor. Architectural search, initialization, nonlinear attention, positional mechanisms, and sparse circuits all affect the gap between representing a function in principle and learning it from data. Capacity alone does not determine which solutions optimization will find.
topic-133-mathrm-nit-scaling-simple-and-.title: Transformer Architecture, Optimization, and Learnability
topic-133-mathrm-nit-scaling-simple-and-.whyItMatters: Understanding that gap can guide cheaper architectures and explain failures that simply increasing size does not resolve. A modification should be judged through both compute use and the tasks or distributions it enables.

topic-134-textttprism-a-3d-probabilistic.evolution: Early examples learn view transitions and qualitative shape from motion. The 2019–2021 papers develop reusable surface structures, differentiable mesh extraction, and hybrid representations. Recent representatives add dynamic text-guided meshes, uncertainty-aware anatomical shapes, and executable CAD generation. This expands the kinds of control sought from a shape model rather than proving one representation best for every task.
openQuestions: How can generated geometry remain editable while allowing topology changes?
What constraints preserve identity and surface consistency through animation?
topic-134-textttprism-a-3d-probabilistic.overview: Three-dimensional shape learning must choose how geometry is stored and manipulated. Implicit fields, explicit meshes, learned surface elements, and hybrid tetrahedral representations make different tradeoffs in topology, detail, correspondence, and editability. The represented methods increasingly connect these forms through differentiable reconstruction and optimization.
topic-134-textttprism-a-3d-probabilistic.title: Learned Shape Representations and Editable Surface Geometry
topic-134-textttprism-a-3d-probabilistic.whyItMatters: A representation suitable for rendering may be awkward for physical editing or temporal consistency. Maintaining a usable surface structure matters when generated assets must be animated, matched across objects, or incorporated into downstream design tools.

topic-135-a-compilation-target-for-proba.evolution: The collection includes early logic-learning and neural proof constructions, followed by 2010s work on lifting, decomposition trees, and sentential decision diagrams. Recent examples connect logical structure to diffusion guidance and classifier compression, while capability-certification results clarify limits of finite tests. These are related uses of logical structure, not an inferred citation lineage.
openQuestions: Which useful query families remain tractable after learning changes the model?
How can approximate symmetry be exploited without overstating exact inference guarantees?
topic-135-a-compilation-target-for-proba.overview: Logical representations can expose repeated structure that makes otherwise expensive inference manageable. This topic includes lifted reasoning over groups of objects, compilation into tractable circuits, and learning models whose supported probability queries are efficient. The choice of representation determines not only speed but which questions can be answered with guarantees.
topic-135-a-compilation-target-for-proba.title: Logical Structure and Tractable Probabilistic Reasoning
topic-135-a-compilation-target-for-proba.whyItMatters: Exploiting symmetry can avoid expanding a compact relational description into an enormous ground model. Explicit tractability also helps distinguish a practical heuristic from a procedure that supports exact counting, conditional queries, or structured constraints.
